text: 壽永二年七月廿四日夜半許、法皇は按察使大納言資方卿の子息右馬頭資時ばかり御伴にて、竊かに御所を出させ給ひ、鞍馬へ御幸なる。鞍馬寺僧ども、「是は猶都近くて惡う候なん」と申間篠の峯藥王坂など云ふ嶮き嶮難を凌がせ給て、横川の解脱谷寂場坊御所になる。大衆起て、「東塔へこそ御幸在べけれ。」と申ければ、東塔の南谷圓融房御所になる。かゝりしかば、衆徒も武士も、圓融房を守護し奉る。法皇は仙洞を出でて天台山に、主上は鳳闕を去て西海へ、攝政殿は芳野の奧とかや。女院宮々は、八幡、賀茂、嵯峨、太秦、西山、東山の片邊りに附て、迯隱させ給へり。平家は落ぬれど、源氏は未だ入替らず。既に此京は主なき里にぞ成にける。開闢より以來、かゝる事あるべしともおぼえず。聖徳太子の未來記にも、今日の事こそ床しけれ。

annotation.translation: In the middle of the night around the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month of the second year of Juei, the Retired Emperor, accompanied only by his son, the Vice-Minister of the Right Horse Office, Suke-toki, son of the Chancellor and Minister of the Right, Daisuke, secretly left the palace and went to Kurama. The monks of Kurama Temple said, "This is still too close to the capital; it is dangerous." They made him cross the steep and difficult passes of Shōno-mine and Yakō-zaka, and he arrived at the residence of the hermitage in the Valley of Deliverance at Yokkawa. The assembly rose and said, "Let us go to the Eastern Tower." Thus, he went to the residence of the priest En'yōbō in the South Valley of the Eastern Tower. Since it was so, both the monks and the samurai guarded En'yōbō. The Retired Emperor left the Sento Palace and went to Tiantai Mountain; the reigning Emperor left the Phoenix Palace and went to the Western Sea; the Regent's residence was in the deep of Yoshino. The Empress Dowager and the Princesses attached themselves to Hachiman, Kamo, Sagano, Fushimi, Nishiyama, and Higashiyama on the outskirts and went into hiding. The Taira had fallen, but the Minamoto had not yet entered. Already, this capital had become a village without a master. Since the creation of the world, it had never been thought that such an event would occur. Even in the Future Record of Prince Shōtoku, today's events were destined to happen.

text: 法皇天台山に渡せ給と聞えさせ給しかば、馳參らせ給ふ人々、其比の入道殿と申は、前關白松殿、當殿とは近衞殿、太政大臣、左右大臣、内大臣、大納言、中納言、宰相、三位、四位、五位の殿上人、すべて世に人とかぞへられ、官加階に望をかけ、所帶所職を帶する程の人の、一人も漏るは無りけり。圓融房には、餘りに參りつどひて、堂上堂下門外門内、隙はさまなく充々たる。山門繁昌門跡の面目とこそ見えたりけれ。

annotation.translation: When they heard that the Retired Emperor had commanded to cross over to Mount Tiantai, the people who rushed to pay their respects came. Among them were the In'ō no Miya, who was the former Kanpaku Matsudono, and the current Dōjōden, along with the Dajō-daijin, the Sadaijin, the Udaijin, the Dainagon, the Chunagon, the Sōnai, and the nobles of the Third, Fourth, and Fifth Ranks; all who were known throughout the world, who held hopes for advancement in their official ranks, and who held various posts and titles, were present without a single omission. At Enmyōbō, the gathering was so excessive that the halls above and below, and inside and outside the gates, were filled without a single gap. It seemed to be a display of the prestige of the Shōmon and the Kōjō.

text: 同廿八日に法皇都へ還御なる。木曾五萬餘騎にて守護し奉る。近江源氏山本の冠者義高、白旗差て先陣に供奉す。此二十餘年見えざりつる白旗の、今日始めて都へ入る、珍しかりし事共なり。

annotation.translation: On the 28th of the same month, the retired emperor returned to the capital. He was guarded by more than 50,000 mounted soldiers from the Kiso clan. Konoe Genji Yamamoto no Gon no Tsukasa Yoshitaka, waving a white banner, led the vanguard in attendance. It was a rare sight that the white banner, which had not been seen for over twenty years, entered the capital for the first time today.

text: 去程に十郎藏人行家、宇治橋を渡て都へ入る。陸奧新判官義康が子、矢田判官代義清、大江山を經て上洛す。攝津國河内の源氏共雲霞の如くに同く都へ亂入る。凡京中には源氏の勢充々たり。勘解由小路中納言經房卿、檢非違使別當左衞門督實家院の殿上の簀子に候て、義仲行家を召す。木曾は赤地の錦の直垂に、唐綾威の鎧著て、いか物作の太刀を帶き、切斑の矢負ひ、滋籐の弓脇に挾み、甲をば脱ぎ高紐にかけて候。十郎藏人は、紺地の錦の直垂に、緋威の鎧著て、金造りの太刀を帶き、大中黒の矢負ひ、塗籠籐の弓脇に挾み、是も甲をば脱ぎ高紐にかけ、ひざまついて候ひけり。前内大臣宗盛公以下、平家の一族追討すべき由仰下さる。兩人庭上に畏て承る。各宿所のなき由を申す。木曾は大膳太夫成忠が宿所、六條西洞院を給はる。十郎藏人は、法住寺殿の南殿と申す萱の御所をぞ給はりける。法皇は主上外戚の平家に取らはれさせ給て、西海の浪の上に漂はせ給ふ事を、御歎き有て、主上竝に三種の神器、都へ返入れ奉るべき由、西國へ院宣を下されたりけれども、平家用ゐ奉らず。

annotation.translation: On the outward journey, Juro-no-Kurando-yukiie crossed Uji Bridge and entered the capital. Yoshimasa, the new judge of Mutsu, and his son Yada-no-Jodai-yoshiyuki, crossed Mount Ooe and came to the capital. The Minamoto of Harima, Kawachi, and others entered the capital in a rush, like clouds and mist. Indeed, the Minamoto's power filled the entire capital. Kanekoji-no-Chunagon-no-Tadafusa, the Minister of the Center, and Kibishishi-no-Betto-no-Saemon-no-Suke-no-Masaie, the Chief of the Ministry of the Right, awaited on the palace veranda of the Imperial Court and summoned Yoshinaka and Yukiie. Kiso wore a crimson brocade hitatare and a karaginu-laced armor, carried a sword of the 'ikamono-zukuri' style, bore cut-patterned arrows, and had a Shitofuji bow tucked at his side; he took off his armor and hung it on a high stand. Juro-no-Kurando wore a dark-blue brocade hitatare and a crimson-laced armor, carried a sword of gold-forged style, bore large-black arrows, and had a lacquered-cage-lace bow tucked at his side; he too took off his armor and hung it on a high stand, then knelt and waited. The former Minister of the Left, Morimori, and below him, the members of the Taira clan were ordered to be exterminated. The two men, bowing in the courtyard, received the order. They reported that they had no lodging. Kiso was granted the lodging of Daizen-no-Tayu-Naritada at Rokujou-nishi-Higashiden. Juro-no-Kurando was granted the thatched imperial residence known as the Southern Palace of Hozan-ji Temple. The Retired Emperor, being taken captive by the Taira, his imperial relatives, and being made to drift upon the waves of the Western Sea, sighed deeply, and although he issued an imperial edict to the Western Provinces ordering that the Emperor and the Three Sacred Regalia be returned to the capital, the Taira did not obey.

text: 高倉院の皇子は、主上の外三所おはしき。二宮をば、儲の君にし奉らんとて、平家いざなひ參らせて、西國へ落給ぬ。三四は都にまし／＼けり。同八月五日、法皇此宮達を迎へ寄せ參らせ給て、先三の宮の五歳に成せ給ふを、「是へ／＼」と仰ければ、法皇を見參させ給ひて大にむつがらせ給ふ間、「とう／＼」とて出し參させ給ひぬ。其後四の宮の四歳に成せ給ふを、「是へ」と仰せければ少も憚らせ給はず、やがて法皇の御膝の上に參せ給ひて、世にも懷氣にぞ坐しける。法皇御涙をはら／＼と流させ給ひて、「げにもすぞろならむ者は、か樣の老法師を見て何とてか懷氣には思ふべき。是ぞ我實の御孫にてぞまし／＼ける。故院の少生に少も違せ給はぬ者哉。かゝる忘れ形見を、今迄見ざりける事よ。」とて、御涙塞あへさせ給はず。淨土寺の二位殿、其時は未丹後殿とて御前に候はせ給ふが、「さて御讓は此宮にてこそ渡らせおはしまし候はめ。」と申させ給へば、法皇「仔細にや。」とぞ仰ける。内々御占のありしにも、「四宮位に即せ給ひてば、百王迄も日本國の御主たるべし。」とぞ勘へ申ける。

annotation.translation: The Prince of Emperor Takakura was one of the three sons of the Sovereign. Regarding the Second Prince, they intended to make him the heir apparent, so the Taira family invited him and he went down to the Western Provinces. Three of them remained in the capital. On the fifth day of the eighth month, the Retired Emperor received and welcomed these three princes to the palace. When the First Prince, now five years old, was told, "Come here," the Retired Emperor had him brought before him, and while he was made to embrace him with great joy, he said, "Come, come," and had him brought forth. Afterward, when the Fourth Prince, now four years old, was told, "Come here," he was not in the least reluctant, and immediately went and sat upon the Retired Emperor's lap, sitting there with such affection that it was rare in the world. The Retired Emperor shed tears profusely, saying, "Indeed, how fortunate must those who are destined to be so be, to see an old monk like me and feel such affection! This is truly my grandson, and he is the one who remained in the capital. Is he not one who bears no resemblance at all to the late Emperor's younger son? What a cherished memory of the late Emperor I have not seen until now!" and he could not restrain his tears. The Lady Nijo of the Jodo Temple, who at that time was still called the Lady of Tango and attended in the palace, said, "Now, the abdication should be passed to this prince." Upon hearing this, the Retired Emperor replied, "Let us consider it carefully." There had been an internal divination which stated, "If the Fourth Prince ascends to the throne, he shall become the sovereign of Japan for a hundred generations." This was the conclusion they reached.

text: 御母儀は七條修理大夫信隆卿の御娘なり。建禮門院の未だ中宮にてまし／＼ける時其御方に宮仕給ひしを、主上常は召れける程に、うち續き宮あまた出來させ給へり。信隆卿、御娘餘たおはしければ、如何にもして女御后にもなしたてまつらばやとねがはれけるに、人の家に白い鷄を千飼つれば、其家に必ず后出來たると云ふ事有りとて、鷄の白いを千そろへて飼はれたりける故にや、此御娘皇子數多生參せ給へり。信隆卿内々うれしうは思はれけれども、平家にも憚り、中宮にも恐れ參せて、もてなし奉る事もおはせざりしを、入道相國の北方八條の二位殿、「苦しかるまじ、我育て參せて、儲の君にして奉らむ。」とて、御乳母共あまた附て、そだて參せ給ひけり。

annotation.translation: Her mother was the daughter of Shijo Shuri no Daiyu Nobutaka. When Kenrei-mon-in was still in the position of Chuugu, she served in her household; as the Emperor frequently summoned her, she continued to bear many children for him. Nobutaka, seeing that his daughter was still so young, prayed that she be made a Nyogo or Kogo in some way. It is said that if a thousand white hens are raised in a household, a queen will surely be born there; thus, because he raised a thousand white hens, this lady gave birth to many princes. Although Nobutaka was inwardly pleased, he feared the Heike clan and the Chuugu, and did not treat her with proper respect. However, the Northern Lady of the Daiso (the Retired Emperor) of Hachijo Ni-i said, 'Do not be troubled; I will raise her and make her a favored consort.' With many wet nurses and attendants attached to her, she was raised by her.

text: 中にも四宮は、二位殿の兄法勝寺執行能圓法師の養君にてぞ坐ける。法印平家に具せられて、西國へ落し時、餘りに遽噪いで、北方をも宮をも京都に棄置參せて下られたりしが、西國より急ぎ人を上せて、「女房宮具し參せて、よく／＼くだり給べし。」と申されたりければ、北方斜ならず悦び、宮いざなひ參せて、西の七條なる處まで出られたりしを、女房の兄紀伊守教光、「是は物の附て狂給ふか。此宮の御運は唯今開かせ給はんずる者を。」とて、取留參せたりける次の日ぞ、法皇より御迎の車參りたりける。何事も然べき事と申ながら四宮の御爲には、紀伊守教光は奉公の人とぞ見えたりける。されども四宮位に即せ給ひて後、其情をも思召し出でさせ給はず、朝恩もなくして年月を送けるが、せめて思ひの餘りにや二首の歌を詠うで、禁中に落書をぞしたりける。

annotation.translation: Among them, Shinisho was a foster son of Noin, the abbot of Hokkaku-ji temple, brother of the Lady of the Second Rank, and he was seated there. When he was incorporated into the Taira clan and fell to the Western Provinces, in his great haste he left the Northern Lady and the Palace behind in Kyoto and descended. However, because he urgently sent a messenger from the Western Provinces saying, 'Send the Palace Lady to us, and let her come down properly,' the Northern Lady, though somewhat displeased, felt joy and invited the Palace, accompanying her as far as the place in the west at Shichijo. The Palace's elder brother, the Governor of Kii, Norimitsu, said, 'Is this a case of possession or madness? It is the one who is about to open the Palace's fortune.' Thus, he detained them. The next day, a carriage for the Emperor's reception arrived from the Daito Emperor. Although it was said that this was the natural course of things, it appeared that Governor Norimitsu of Kii was a loyal retainer in the service of Shinisho. However, after Shinisho ascended to the throne, he did not recall their feelings or show them favor, and passed the years without receiving imperial favor. Yet, perhaps overwhelmed by his thoughts, he composed two poems and dropped them into the Forbidden Palace.

text: 主上是を叡覽あて「あな無慚や、されば未だ世に長らへてありけるな。今日まで是を思召寄らざりけるこそ愚なれ。」とて、朝恩蒙り、正三位に敍せられけるとぞ聞えし。

annotation.translation: The Emperor gazed upon this and said, "Alas, how shameless! It is precisely because you have yet remained alive in this world that you are so foolish." Thus, having received a morning audience, it is said that he was promoted to Junior Third Rank.

text: 同八月十日、院の殿上にて除目行はる。木曾は左馬頭に成て、越後國を給はる。其上朝日の將軍と云ふ院宣を下されけり。十郎藏人は備後守に成る。木曾は越後をきらへば伊豫をたぶ。十郎藏人備後を嫌へば備前を給ぶ。其外源氏十餘人、受領、檢非違使、靱負尉、兵衞尉に成れけり。

annotation.translation: On the same tenth day of the eighth month, the appointment ceremony was held in the Emperor's palace. Kiso became Left Horse Master and was given Echigo Province. Moreover, an imperial edict was issued declaring him the Morning Sun General. Juro-no-Kurando became Bitchu-no-kami. Since Kiso disliked Echigo, Iyo was granted to him. Since Juro-no-Kurando disliked Bitchu, Bizen was granted to him. The other members of the Minamoto clan, more than ten persons, became provincial governors, Keniwa-shi, Yuburi-no-jo, and Hei-no-jo.

text: 同十六日、平家の一門百六十餘人が官職を停て、殿上の御札を削らる。其中に、平大納言時忠卿、内藏頭信基、讃岐中將時實、是三人は削られず。其は主上幵に三種の神器都へ返入れ奉るべき由、彼時忠卿の許へ度々院宣を下されけるに依て也。

annotation.translation: On the sixteenth day of the same month, over 160 members of the Taira clan were dismissed from their official posts, and their names were removed from the registers of courtiers. This was because, in order to return the Three Sacred Treasures to the capital along with the Emperor, the Emperor's decree was repeatedly issued to Counselor Tokitada's residence.

text: 同廿日、都には法皇の宣命にて、四宮閑院殿にて位に即せ給ふ。攝政は本の攝政近衞殿、替らせ給はず、頭や藏人成置きて、人々皆退出せられけり。三の宮の御乳母泣悲み後悔すれども甲斐ぞなき。天に二の日なし、國に二人の王なしとは申せども、平家の惡行に依てこそ、京田舎に二人の王は坐けれ。

annotation.translation: On the same 20th day, by imperial edict in the capital, the Fourth Palace, Kan'in-den, ascended the throne. The Regent remained the original Regent, Konoe-dono; he was not replaced. Officials such as the Kampaku and Kubo were appointed, and all others withdrew. Even the Third Palace's wet nurse wept and repented, but it was in vain. Though it is said that there is no second day in heaven and no second king in the land, it was precisely because of the evil deeds of the Taira clan that two kings were seated in the capital and the provinces.

text: 昔文徳天皇は天安二年八月二十三日に隱れさせ給ひぬ。御子の宮達あまた位に望を懸て坐ますは内々御祈とも有けり。一の御子惟高親王をば、小原皇子とも申き。王者の才量を御心に懸け、四海の安危は掌の中に照し、百王の理亂は心の中にかけ給へり。されば賢聖の名をも取せ坐ぬべき君なりと見え給へり。二宮惟仁親王は、其比の執柄忠仁公の御娘、染殿の后の御腹也。一門公卿列して持成奉り給ひしかば、是も差置き難き御事なり。彼は守文繼體の器量有り。是は萬機輔佐の臣相有り。彼も是も痛はしくて、何れも思召煩れき。一宮惟高親王の御祈は、柿本紀僧正信濟とて、東寺の一の長者、弘法大師の御弟子也。二宮惟仁親王の御祈には、外祖忠仁公の御持僧、比叡山の惠亮和尚ぞ承はられける。互に劣らぬ高僧達也。とみに事行難うや有んずらんと人々ささやきあへり。御門隱させ給しかば、公卿僉議有り。「抑臣等が、慮を以て、選んで位に即奉ん事、用捨私有に似たり、萬人唇を反べし。しらず、競馬相撲の節を遂げて其運を知り、雌雄に依て、寶祚を授け奉るべし。」と議定畢ぬ。

annotation.translation: In the past, Emperor Montoku was hidden on the 23rd day of the 8th month of the 2nd year of Tengyō. His many sons, who sat with their hopes placed on attaining the throne, had, in private, an imperial prayer. One of his sons, Prince Taka, was also called Kōhara no Ōji. He had the royal talent and capacity in his mind; the safety and peril of the four seas were within the palm of his hand, and the order and disorder of a hundred kings were in his heart. Thus, he appeared to be a sovereign worthy of the name of a sage and wise man. The second prince, Prince Tada, was the son of the daughter of Lord Tadahito of that time, the consort of the Shinden palace. The nobles of the imperial house lined up and offered support to Mochinari, so this was also a matter difficult to disregard. He had the capacity of a successor to the throne; this one had the qualities of a minister to assist in the affairs of state. Both were painful to him, and he was troubled by thoughts of both. The prayer for the first prince, Prince Taka, was conducted by the monk Shinsai of the Kakinomoto clan, a senior priest of Tō-ji and a disciple of Kōbō Daishi. The prayer for the second prince, Prince Tada, was conducted by the priest of his maternal grandfather, Lord Tadahito, and the monk Eryō of Mount Hiei. They were both eminent monks, equal in stature. People whispered among themselves that it would be difficult to proceed with the matter. When the imperial gate was closed, the nobles held a joint deliberation. "At first, if we, using our judgment, choose and present him to the throne, it would resemble private favoritism in appointment and dismissal, and would cause all people to turn their lips in criticism. Rather, let us finish the customs of horse racing and sumo, know the fortune, and, depending on the outcome, bestow the imperial succession." The deliberation was concluded thus.

text: 同九月二日二人の宮達右近馬場へ行啓有り。爰に王公卿相、花の袂を粧ひ、玉の轡を竝べ、雲の如に重なり、星の如くに列り給ひしかば、此事希代の勝事、天下の壯なるみもの、日來心を寄奉りし月卿雲客、兩方に引分て、手を握り心を碎き給へり。御祈の高僧達、何れか疎略あらむや。信濟は東寺に壇を立て、惠亮は大内の眞言院に壇を立て行なはれけるに、惠亮は失たりと云ふ披露をなさば信濟僧正たゆむ心もやあるらんとて、惠亮和尚失たりといふ披露を成し、肝膽を碎いて祈れけり。既に十番の競馬始る。始め四番は一の宮惟高親王勝せ給ふ。後六番は二の宮惟仁親王勝せ給ふ。やがて相撲の節有るべしとて、惟高の御方より、名虎右兵衞督とて、六十人が力現したるゆゝしき人をぞ出されたる。惟仁親王家よりは、能雄少將とて、背小うたへにして、片手に合べしとも見えぬ人、御夢想の御告有とて、申請けてぞいでられたる。名虎、能雄寄合うて、ひし／＼とつま取して退にけり。暫し有て名虎、能雄少將を取てさゝげて、二丈許ぞ投たりける。たゞなほて倒れず。能雄又つと寄り、えい聲を上て名虎を取て伏むとす。名虎もともに聲をいだして能雄をとてふせむとす。何れ劣れりとも見えず。されども、名虎大の男、かさに廻る。能雄は危なう見えければ、二宮惟仁親王家の御母儀染殿后より、御使櫛の齒の如く、走り重て、「御方すでに劣色に見ゆ。如何せむ。」と[1]仰けれは、惠亮和尚、大威徳の法を修せられけるが、「こは心憂事にこそ。」とて、獨鈷を以て腦を撞碎き、乳に和して護摩に燒き、黒烟を立て、一揉揉まれたりければ、能雄相撲に勝にけり。親王位に即せ給ふ。清和御門是なり。後には水尾天皇とぞ申ける。其よりしてこそ山門には聊の事にも、惠亮腦を碎けば、二帝位に即き給ひ、尊位智劍を振しかば、菅相納受し給ふとも傳たれ。是のみや法力にても有けん。其外は皆天照大神の御はからひとぞ承はる。平家は西國にて是を傳聞きぬ。「安からぬ。三宮をも四宮をも取參せて落下べかりしものを。」と後悔せられければ、平大納言時忠卿、「さらむには木曾が主にしたてまつたる高倉宮の御子を、御乳母讃岐守重秀が、御出家せさせ奉り、具し參せて北國へ落下りしこそ、位には即け給はんずらめ」と宣へば、又或人々の申されけるは、「それは出家の宮をばいかゞ、位に即奉るべき。」時忠「さもさうず、還俗の國王の樣、異國にも先蹤有らん、我朝には先天武天皇未だ東宮の御時、大伴皇子に憚からせ給て、鬢髮を剃り、芳野の奧に忍ばせ給せたりしかども、大伴皇子を亡して、終には位に即せ給ひき。又孝謙天皇も、大菩提心を發し、御飾をおろさせ給ひ、御名をば法基尼と申しかども、再位に即て、稱徳天皇と申しぞかし。まして木曾が主にし奉りたる還俗の宮、仔細在まじ。」とぞ宣ひける。

annotation.translation: On the second day of the ninth month, the two princes traveled to the Right Stable. There, the nobles and high ministers adorned themselves with floral sleeves and aligned jade reins, gathering like clouds and standing in rows like stars. Since this was a rare and magnificent event, a wonder of the world, and the moon-like ministers and cloud-like guests, who had devoted their hearts for some time, were divided into two sides, grasping hands and breaking their hearts in sorrow. Which of the great monks offering prayers would be negligent? Shinzei established an altar at the Eastern Temple, and Eryo established an altar at the Esoteric Hall within the Inner Palace, where the rites were performed. When Eryo announced his failure, Shinzei the High Priest thought, "Perhaps he is losing heart," and thus Eryo the Monk made the announcement of failure, breaking his heart and praying. Then the tenth horse race began. In the first four races, Prince Takamichi of the First Palace won. In the latter six races, Prince Tadanobu of the Second Palace won. Soon there would be a sumo match. From the side of Takamichi, a mighty man named Toru Uemon-no-kami was sent forth, sixty men strong. From the side of Prince Tadanobu, a minor official named Nao-o was sent, a small man with a slender back, appearing unable to even clasp hands with one hand, and was dispatched with a dream oracle. Toru and Nao-o grappled and struggled fiercely, retreating briefly. After a moment, Toru lifted Nao-o the Minor Official and threw him about two jō high. Yet he did not fall. Nao-o again approached, shouting loudly, and attempted to throw Toru down. Toru also shouted and tried to counter Nao-o. Neither seemed inferior. However, Toru was a large man and spun around. Seeing Nao-o in danger, the mother of the Second Prince Tadanobu, the Empress Someiden, sent messengers like combs, running swiftly, saying, "Your side already appears inferior. What shall be done?" Hearing this, the monk Eryo, who had cultivated the great Vajradhara Dharma, thought, "This is a matter of deep anxiety." He struck his own head with a single vajra, crushed it, mixed the brain with milk, burned it in a fire offering, raised black smoke, and kneaded it thoroughly. Consequently, Nao-o won the sumo match. The Prince ascended to the throne. This is Emperor Seiwa of the Seiwa Gate. Later he was called Emperor Toba. From that time onward, it is said that at Mount Hiei, whenever Eryo had his head crushed, two emperors ascended to the throne, and the Vajra of Wisdom was brandished, with the Minister of the Right accepting it. Is it due to magical power? Or is it solely the providence of Amaterasu Ōmikami? The Taira family heard this story in the Western Provinces. "It is unsettling. We should have taken both the Third and Fourth Princes and cast them down." Regretting this, Minister of the Left Taira no Tokitada said, "If that is so, let the son of Prince Takakura, who is the master of Kiso, be taken by his wet nurse, the Governor of Sanuki, Shigehide, who has him tonsured and sent him north to the capital, so that he may ascend the throne." Others replied, "How can a tonsured prince ascend the throne?" Tokitada said, "Indeed, there are precedents in foreign lands for kings who return to secular life. In our own court, Emperor Tenmu, while still Crown Prince, was compelled by Prince Ōtomo to shave his hair and hide him in the depths of Yoshino, but after Prince Ōtomo's death, he eventually ascended the throne. Similarly, Empress Genmei, having generated the great Bodhi mind, removed her ornaments and took the name Hōken, yet she ascended the throne again and was known as Empress Shōtoku. Moreover, the tonsured prince, who is the master of Kiso, surely has the qualifications." This was the declaration.

annotation.translation: Thus it became late September, about ten days past. On the evening of the autumn gale that strips the reed leaves, on the bed where Dokumaru sleeps, his sleeve, once a single cloth, has become tattered. The profound sadness of deep autumn, though one might say nothing, is indeed difficult to endure on a journey. On the thirteenth night of September, though it is a moon that has earned a name, that night, tears welling up from thoughts of the capital cloud over it, and it does not shine clearly. text: 豐後國は刑部卿三位頼資卿の國也けり。子息頼經朝臣を代官に置かれたり。京より頼經の許へ、平家は神明にも放たれ奉り、君にも捨られ參せて、帝都を出で、浪の上に漂ふ落人となれり。然を鎭西の者共が請取て、もてなすこそ奇怪なれ。當國に於ては從ふべからず。一味同心して、追出すべき由、宣ひ遣されたりければ、頼經朝臣是を當國の住人緒方三郎維義に下知す。

annotation.translation: Bungo Province was the domain of Minister of Punishments Rank Third, Yorimasa. His son, Yoritsune, was appointed as the deputy. The Taira clan, having been abandoned even by the deities and forsaken by the sovereign, left the imperial capital and became outlaws drifting upon the waves. Yet the people of Chikuzen requested them and showed them hospitality, which was strange. They should not be obeyed in this province. Since they were ordered to act with one mind and drive them out, Yoritsune conveyed this command to the local resident, Ogata Saburō Yoshiyoshi.

text: 彼維義は、怖き者の末なりけり。。譬へば豐後國の片山里に昔女有りけり。或人の一人娘、夫も無りけるが許へ母にも知せず、男夜な夜な通ふ程に、年月も重なる程に、身も只ならず成ぬ。母是を怪しむで、「汝が許へ通ふ者は、何者ぞ。」と問へば、「來るをば見れども、歸るをば知らず。」とぞいひける。「さらば男の歸らん時、驗しを附て行む方を繋いで見よ。」とぞ教へければ、娘母の教に從て、朝歸りする男の水色の狩衣を著たりけるに狩衣のくびがみに、針を刺し、賤の小手卷といふ物を著て、歴て行方を繋いで行けば、豐後國に取ても、日向境、姥嶽と云ふ嵩のすそ、大きなる岩屋の中へぞ繋ぎ入たる。女岩屋の口にたゝずんで聞けば、大きなる聲してぞによびける。「わらはこそ是まで尋參たれ、見參せむ。」と云ければ、我は是人の姿にはあらず、汝我姿を見ては、肝魂も身に副まじき也。とう／＼歸れ。汝が孕める子は、男子なるべし。弓矢打物取て、九州二島にならぶ者も有まじきぞ。」といひける。女重て申けるは、「縱如何なる姿にても有れ、日ごろの好などか忘るべき、互に姿をも見もし見えむ。」といはれて、「さらば。」とて、岩屋の中より臥長は五六尺、跡枕べは十四五丈も有らんと覺る大蛇にて、動搖してこそ這出たれ。狩衣のくびがみに刺すと思つる針は、即大蛇ののどぶえにこそ差いたりけれ。女是を見て肝魂も身にそはず、引具したる所從十餘人倒れふためき喚叫んで逃去ぬ。女歸て、程なく産をしたりければ、男子にてぞ有ける。母方の祖父大太夫生立て見むとて生立たれば、未十歳にも滿ざるに、背大に顏長く長高かりけり。七歳にて元服せさせ、母方の祖父を、大太夫といふ間、是をば大太とこそ附たりけれ。夏も冬も、手足に大きなる胝隙なくわれければ、胝大太とこそいはれけれ。件の大蛇は日向國に崇められ給へる高知尾の明神の神體是也。此緒方の三郎はあかがり大太には五代の孫也。かゝる怖ろしき者の末なりければ國司の仰せを院宣と號して九州二島に囘し文をしければ然るべき兵共維義に隨ひ付く。

annotation.translation: Heike no Yoshitsune was the descendant of a terrible being. For instance, in the past, there was a woman in Katayama, Bungo Province. She had a daughter from a certain man, though she had no husband; without her mother's knowledge, a man came to her every night, and as the years passed, she became pregnant. Her mother grew suspicious and asked, 'Who is the one you are visiting?' The daughter replied, 'I see him when he comes, but I do not know where he goes.' The mother then instructed, 'Then, when the man is about to return, tie a token to him to see where he goes.' Following her mother's advice, the daughter wore a blue hunting robe, inserted a needle into the collar of the robe, and dressed in a humble hand-woven sleeve cover, then tied a string to him to follow his path. He went all the way to Bungo Province, to the border of Hyuga Province, to the foot of a mountain called Uba-dake, and entered a large cave. The woman stood at the mouth of the cave and listened; a great voice called out, 'I have searched for you up to this point and will now reveal myself.' Then he said, 'I am not in this human form; if you were to see my true form, your soul would not remain in your body. Go back quickly. The child you carry will be a boy. He will wield a bow and arrows, and no one in the two islands of Kyushu will equal him.' The woman replied again, 'No matter what form you take, I would never forget our past love; I wish to see your form.' Upon hearing this, from within the cave emerged a great snake, five or six shaku in length when lying down, with a distance of fifteen to twenty shaku to its tail, moving and writhing. The needle she thought was stuck in the collar of the hunting robe was actually embedded in the snake's throat. Seeing this, the woman's soul fled her body, and her attendants, over ten in number, fell down, groaning, crying out, and fled in terror. The woman returned home and soon gave birth to a son. Her maternal grandfather, Odaibu, had the child born so that he might see him. Before the boy reached ten years of age, his back was tall, his face long, and his stature great. At seven, he underwent the coming-of-age ceremony. Because his maternal grandfather was called Odaibu, the boy was given the name 'Oda.' Whether in summer or winter, calluses formed on his hands and feet without any gaps, so he was called 'Callus Oda.' That great snake is the physical form of Takachio-no-Myojin, a deity revered in Hyuga Province. This Oda no Sanro was the fifth-generation grandson of Akagari Oda. Since he was the descendant of such a terrifying being, the Provincial Governor issued an imperial edict, and a return letter was sent to the two islands of Kyushu, causing soldiers worthy of the task to follow Yoshitsune.

text: 平家いまは筑紫に都を定め、内裏造るべきよし沙汰ありしに維義が謀反と聞えしかば、こは如何と噪がれけり。平大納言時忠卿申されけるは、「彼維義は、小松殿の御家人也。小松殿の君達一所向はせ給ひて、こしらへて御覽ぜらるべうや候らん。」と申されければ、誠にもとて、小松の新三位中將資盛卿五百餘騎で豐後國に打越えて樣々にこしらへ給へども、維義從奉らず。剩へ「君達をも、只今爰で取籠參すべう候へども、大事の中の小事なれとて、取籠參らせずは、何程の事か渡せ給ふべき。とう／＼太宰府へ歸らせ給ひて、只御一所で如何にも成せ給へ。」とて、追返し奉る。維義が次男、野尻次郎維村を使者で、太宰府へ申けるは、「平家は重恩の君にてましませば、甲を脱ぎ弦を弛いて參るべう候へども、一院の御定に速に九國内を逐出し參らせよと候。急ぎ出させ給ふべうや候らん。」と申送たりければ、平大納言時忠卿、緋緒括の袴、絲葛の直垂、立烏帽子で、維村に出向て宣けるは、「夫我君は、天孫四十九世の正統、人王八十一代の御門也。天照大神正八幡宮も、吾君をこそ守り參させ給らめ。就中に故太政大臣入道殿は保元平治兩度の逆亂を靜め、其上鎭西の者どもをばうち樣にこそ召されしか。東國北國の凶徒等が頼朝義仲等に語らはれて、爲おほせたらば國を預けう、庄をたばんといふを、實と思ひて、其鼻豐後が下知に從はん事、然べからず。」とぞ宣ける。豐後國司刑部卿三位頼資卿は、究て鼻の大きにおはしければ、かうは宣けり。維村歸て、父に此由云ければ、「こは如何に、昔は昔今は今、其儀ならば、速に九國の中を逐出し奉れ。」とて、勢汰ふるなど聞えしかば、平家の侍源太夫判官季定、攝津判官守澄、「向後傍輩のため奇怪に候。召取候はん。」とて、其勢三千餘騎で、筑後國、高野本庄に發向して、一日一夜攻戰ふ。されども維義が勢、雲霞の如く重りければ、力及ばで引退く。

annotation.translation: The Heike, now having established the capital at Tsukushi, were in the process of constructing the Imperial Palace, but when it was heard that Ieyoshi had plotted a rebellion, there was great clamor over what to do. The Great Counselor Tokitada said, 'That Ieyoshi is a retainer of the Lord of Komatsu. If the Lord and his ladies were to gather together and prepare something, would they not be able to see it?' Thus he spoke, and indeed, the new Third Rank Captain of the Inner Palace, Sane-mori, crossed over to Bungo Province with over five hundred horsemen, making various preparations, but Ieyoshi did not obey. Instead, he said, 'Although we could take the Lord and his ladies into confinement right here, as this is a minor matter within a major one, if we do not confine them, what could be the extent of their passage? Let them return to Dazaifu in confusion, and let them do whatever they wish in their single dwelling.' Thus he sent them back. Ieyoshi's second son, Nojiri Jiro Iemura, went as an envoy to Dazaifu and said, 'Since the Heike are lords of great grace, we could lay down our armor and relax our bows, but by the Emperor's decree, we are to swiftly expel the nine provinces. Could we not be ordered to set out at once?' Thus he delivered his message. The Great Counselor Tokitada, wearing a purple-sashed hakama, a silk-crepe kosode, and a standing eboshi, went out to meet Iemura and declared, 'Our Lord is the legitimate successor of the Heavenly Grandson for forty-nine generations, the imperial house of eighty-one reigns. Even the Amaterasu-Omikami and the Hachiman-gu Shrine itself must surely protect our Lord. In particular, the late Dajō-daijin, who had entered the priesthood, quelled the rebellions of Hogen and Heiji on two occasions, and thereupon he summoned the men of Chikushi and dealt with them thoroughly. The villains of the Eastern and Northern provinces, such as Yoritomo and Yoshinaka, have been spoken to by them; if they were to be commanded by their orders, they would entrust the provinces and seize the manors. To believe this as truth and to obey the decree issued from Bungo is impossible.' Thus he declared. The Governor of Bungo Province, the Minister of Punishments, the Third Rank Yorinari, ultimately, with his nose greatly swollen, said this. Iemura returned and reported this to his father. His father said, 'How can this be? The past is the past, and the present is the present; if this is the case, let us swiftly expel the nine provinces.' Thus, the noise of battle was heard. The Heike warriors, Gen no Jūbu no Kanjō, and Settsu no Kanjō, Moru, said, 'In the future, strange things may happen for the sake of our companions. Let us summon them.' Thus, with a force of over three thousand horsemen, they set out from Chikugo Province to Takano Honjo and attacked for one day and one night. However, Ieyoshi's forces were as dense as clouds and mist, and their strength was insufficient, so they retreated.

text: 平家は緒方の三郎維義が三萬餘騎の勢にて、既に寄すと聞えしかば、取物も取あへず、太宰府をこそ落給へ。さしも憑しかりつる天滿天神の注連の邊を心細も立離れ、駕輿丁も無れば、葱花鳳輦は唯名のみ聞きて、主上腰輿にぞ召れける。國母を始め奉て、止事なき女房達、袴の裾を取り大臣殿以下の卿相雲客、指貫のそば挾み、水城の戸を出で、歩跣にて我さきに前にと、箱崎の津へこそ落給へ。折節降る雨車軸の如し、吹く風砂をあぐとかや。落る涙降る雨、分きて何れも見えざりけり。住吉、箱崎、香椎、宗像、伏拜み、唯主上舊都の還幸とのみぞ祈られける。たるみ山、鶉濱などいふ峨々たる嶮難を凌ぎ渺々たる平沙へぞ趣き給ふ。何つ習はしの御事なれば、御足より出づる血は砂を染め、紅の袴は色をまし、白袴はすそ紅にぞなりにける。彼玄弉三藏の流沙葱嶺を凌れけん苦も、是には爭かまさるべき。されども其は求法の爲なれば、自他の利益も有けん。是は怨敵の故なれば、後世の苦、且思ふこそ悲けれ。原田大夫種直は二千餘騎で平家の御ともにまゐる。山鹿兵藤次秀遠數千騎で平家の御むかひにまゐりけるが、種直秀遠以外に不和になりければ、種直はあしかりなんとて道より引かへす。あし屋の津といふ處をすぎさせ給ふにもこれは我が都より福原へ通し時、里の名なればとていづれの里よりもなつかしう今更あはれをぞもよほされける。新羅、百濟、高麗、契丹、雲の終海の終迄も、落行ばやとはおぼしけれども波風向うて叶はねば、兵藤次秀遠に具せられて、山賀城にぞ籠り給ふ。山賀へも又敵寄すと聞えしかば、小舟共に召て、通夜豐前國、柳浦へぞ渡り給ふ。爰に、内裏造るべき由沙汰有しかども、分限無かりければ造られず。又長門より源氏寄と聞えしかば、海士小舟に取乘て、海にぞ浮び給ひける。

annotation.translation: The Heike were told that Jōgata no Saburō Ieyoshi had arrived with a force of over thirty thousand cavalry, so, unable even to gather their belongings, they resolved to abandon Dazaifu. Even the sacred rope boundary of the Amaterasu shrine at Tenmangu, which they had held so dear, was left behind in a state of sorrow; without bearers to carry the palanquin, the phoenix-dragon palanquin was heard of only by name, and the Emperor was summoned into a simple waist-carriage. Accompanied by the Imperial Mother, ladies-in-waiting without any particular reason, and ministers and high officials below the rank of Minister, who held the hems of their hakama and had their sleeves tucked in, they passed through the gates of the Mizuki fortress, barefoot and urging one another to go ahead, resolving to flee to the port of Hakozaki. The rain that fell at that moment was like the wheels of a cart; the wind blew sand as if it were a storm. Tears fell like rain, and it was impossible to distinguish which was which. They prayed only to the shrines of Sumiyoshi, Hakozaki, Kashii, Munakata, and Fukuhai, that the Emperor might return to the old capital. They crossed the towering, rugged passes of Tarumi and Uzuhama and proceeded toward the vast, boundless plain sands. Since this was an unprecedented event, the blood flowing from the Emperor's feet stained the sand, the red hakama deepened in color, and the white hakama turned red at the hem. The suffering endured by the monk Gen'e when he crossed the flowing sands and the葱岭 (葱嶺) was nothing compared to this. Yet, since his journey was for the sake of seeking the Dharma, it brought benefit to both self and others. But this was because of an enemy; the suffering of future generations, even if merely thought of, is indeed sorrowful. Harada no Daisuke Tanechika came with over two thousand cavalry to join the Heike. Yamaga no Hyōjōji Hidenobu came with several thousand cavalry to oppose the Heike, but apart from Tanechika and Hidenobu, discord arose, so Tanechika turned back from the road, saying it would be unwise. Even when they passed the place called Ashiya-no-tsu, it was as though they were returning from their capital to Fukuhara; because it was the name of a local village, they felt more nostalgia than for any other village, and now more than ever, their hearts were moved to tears. From Silla, Baekje, Goryeo, and Khitan, from the end of the clouds to the end of the sea, they wished to flee, but the waves and wind turned against them, so they were surrounded by Hyōjōji Hidenobu and took refuge in Yamaga Castle. Hearing that enemies were approaching Yamaga as well, they summoned small boats and crossed to Yūka in Bungo Province. There, though there were plans to construct a new palace, it could not be built due to lack of funds. Furthermore, hearing that the Minamoto were approaching from Nagato, they boarded fishing boats and floated out onto the sea.

Accompanied by the Imperial Mother, ladies-in-waiting without any particular reason, and ministers and high officials below the rank of Minister, who held the hems of their hakama and had their sleeves tucked in, they passed through the gates of the Mizuki fortress, barefoot and urging one another to go ahead, resolving to flee to the port of Hakozaki. The rain that fell at that moment was like the wheels of a cart; the wind blew sand as if it were a storm. Tears fell like rain, and it was impossible to distinguish which was which. They prayed only to the shrines of Sumiyoshi, Hakozaki, Kashii, Munakata, and Fukuhai, that the Emperor might return to the old capital. They crossed the towering, rugged passes of Tarumi and Uzuhama and proceeded toward the vast, boundless plain sands. Since this was an unprecedented event, the blood flowing from the Emperor's feet stained the sand, the red hakama deepened in color, and the white hakama turned red at the hem. The suffering endured by the monk Gen'e when he crossed the flowing sands and the葱岭 (葱嶺) was nothing compared to this. Yet, since his journey was for the sake of seeking the Dharma, it brought benefit to both self and others. But this was because of an enemy; the suffering of future generations, even if merely thought of, is indeed sorrowful. Harada no Daisuke Tanechika came with over two thousand cavalry to join the Heike. Yamaga no Hyōjōji Hidenobu came with several thousand cavalry to oppose the Heike, but apart from Tanechika and Hidenobu, discord arose, so Tanechika turned back from the road, saying it would be unwise. Even when they passed the place called Ashiya-no-tsu, it was as though they were returning from their capital to Fukuhara; because it was the name of a local village, they felt more nostalgia than for any other village, and now more than ever, their hearts were moved to tears. From Silla, Baekje, Goryeo, and Khitan, from the end of the clouds to the end of the sea, they wished to flee, but the waves and wind turned against them, so they were surrounded by Hyōjōji Hidenobu and took refuge in Yamaga Castle. Hearing that enemies were approaching Yamaga as well, they summoned small boats and crossed to Yūka in Bungo Province. There, though there were plans to construct a new palace, it could not be built due to lack of funds. Furthermore, hearing that the Minamoto were approaching from Nagato, they boarded fishing boats and floated out onto the sea.

text: 小松殿の三男、左の中將清經は、本より何事も思入れける人なれば「都をば源氏が爲に攻落され、鎭西をば維義が爲に追出さる。網に懸れる魚の如し。何くへ行かば遁べきかは。長らへ果べき身にもあらず。」とて、月の夜心を澄し舟の屋形に立出て、横笛音取朗詠して、遊ばれけるが、閑に經讀み念佛して、海にぞ沈み給ひける。男女泣悲めども甲斐ぞなき。

annotation.translation: Kotomatsu-no-dono's third son, the Left Midshipman Kiyotsune, being a man who thought deeply about everything from the beginning, said, 'The capital has been attacked and fallen for the sake of the Minamoto, and Chikuzen has been expelled for the sake of Yoritomo. It is like a fish caught in a net. Where could one flee to? I am not even fit to live.' So, he cleared his heart on a moonlit night, stepped out onto the cabin of a boat, played the flute, sang loudly, and enjoyed himself; but later, in idleness, he read scriptures, recited the nembutsu, and sank into the sea. Men and women wept in sorrow, but it was in vain.

text: 長門國は新中納言知盛卿の國なりけり。目代は紀伊刑部大夫通資と云ふ者也。平家の、小船どもに乘り給へる由承て、大船百餘艘點じて奉る。平家是に乘移り、四國の地へぞ渡られける。重能が沙汰として、四國の内を催して讃岐の八島にかたの樣なる板屋の内裏や、御所をぞ造せける。其程は怪の民屋を皇居とするに及ばねば、船を御所とぞ定めける。大臣殿以下の卿相雲客、海士の蓬屋に日を送り、賤がふしどに夜を重ね、龍頭鷁首を海中に浮べ、浪の上の行宮は、靜なる時なし。月を浸せる潮の深き愁に沈み、霜を掩へる葦の葉の脆き命を危ぶむ。洲崎に騒ぐ千鳥の聲は、曉の恨をまし、そはゐにかゝるかぢの音、夜半に心を傷しむ。遠松に白鷺のむれ居るを見ては、源氏の旗を擧るかと疑ひ、野雁の遼海に鳴を聞ては、兵共の終夜船を漕かと驚かる。晴嵐肌を侵し、翠黛紅顏の色漸々衰、蒼波眼穿て、外土望郷の涙押へがたし。翠帳紅閨にかはれるは、土生の小屋の葦簾、薫爐の煙に異る蘆火燒く屋の賤きに附ても、女房達盡せぬもの思ひに、紅の涙塞敢ず、緑の黛亂つゝ、其人とも見え給はず。

annotation.translation: Nagato Province was the domain of the newly appointed Middle Counselor Tomomori, my lord. The provincial governor was Kii no Daibu Tsuneyasu, as they say. Hearing that the Heike clan were boarding small boats, they counted and presented over one hundred large ships. The Heike clan boarded them and crossed over to the land of Shikoku. As ordered by Shigenobu, they gathered in Shikoku and constructed a board-house resembling the Inner Palace or the Imperial Residence at the Eight Islands of Sanuki. At that time, since it was not yet time to make the strange people's house the Imperial Palace, they decided to make the ships the Imperial Residence. The ministers, lords, and nobles below the Minister, spending days in the fishermen's thatched huts, and passing nights in the humble dwellings of the lowly, raised the dragon-head and goose-head ships to float upon the sea; the moving palace upon the waves knew no quiet moment. Sinking into the deep sorrow of the tide that soaks the moon, fearing the fragile life of the reed leaves that cover the frost. The cry of thousand plovers stirring at Saki heightens the resentment of dawn; the sound of the oar blades, so strangely placed, wounds the heart in the middle of the night. Seeing the flock of white herons dwelling in the distant pines, they suspect that the Minamoto flags are raised; hearing the cry of wild geese over the vast sea, they are startled, thinking the soldiers are rowing the ships all night. The clear mist invades the skin; the colors of the green eyebrows and rosy faces gradually fade; gazing at the blue waves until the eyes wear out, the tears of longing for one's native soil beyond the borders cannot be held back. When the green curtains and red chambers are replaced by the rush mats of the humble huts of the earth-born, even if one attaches oneself to the lowly house burning reeds, different from the smoke of the incense burner, the ladies, overcome by unfulfilled thoughts, cannot help but block their red tears; their green eyebrows grow disordered, and they no longer appear to be themselves.

text: さる程に鎌倉前右兵衞佐頼朝、居ながら征夷將軍の院宣を蒙る。御使は左史生中原泰定とぞ聞えし。十月十四日關東へ下著す。兵衞佐宣ひけるは、「頼朝年來勅勘を蒙たりしかども、今武勇の名譽長ぜるに依て、居ながら征夷將軍の院宣を蒙る。如何んが私で請取奉るべき。若宮の社にて、給はらん。」とて、若宮へ參り向はれけり。八幡は鶴岡に立せ給へり。地形石清水に違ず、廻廊有り、樓門有り、作路十餘町見下たり。「抑院宣をば、誰してか請取り奉るべき。」とて評定有り。三浦介義澄して請取奉るべし。其故は、八箇國に聞えたりし弓矢取、三浦平太郎爲嗣が末葉也。其上父大介は君の御爲に命を捨たる兵なれば、彼義明が黄泉の冥闇を照さんが爲とぞ聞えし。院宣の御使泰定は、家子二人郎等十人具したり。院宣をば文袋に入て雜色が頸にぞ懸させたりける。三浦介義澄も家子二人郎等十人具したり。二人の家子は、和田三郎宗實、比企藤四郎能員なり。十人の郎等をば大名十人して、俄に一人づゝ仕立けり。三浦介がその日の裝束にはかちの直垂に、黒絲威の鎧著て、いか物造の大太刀はき、廿四差たる大中黒の矢負ひ、滋籐の弓脇に挾み、甲をば脱ぎ高紐にかけ、腰を曲めて院宣を請取る。泰定「院宣を請取奉る人は如何なる人ぞ、名乘れや。」と云ければ、三浦介とは名乘らで、本名を三浦の荒次郎義澄とこそ名乘たれ。院宣をばらん箱に入られたり。兵衞佐に奉る。稍有てらん箱をば返されけり。重かりければ、泰定是を明て見るに、砂金百兩入られたり。若宮の拜殿にして、泰定に酒を勸らる。齋院次官親義陪膳す。五位一人役送を勤む。馬三匹引かる。一匹に鞍置たり。大宮の侍狩野工藤一臈資經是を引く。古き萱屋をしつらうて、いれられたり。厚綿の衣二兩、小袖十重長持に入て設たり、紺藍摺白布千端を積めり。杯盤豐にして美麗なり。

annotation.translation: In this manner, Kamakura's former Right War Commander Yoritomo received the Imperial Decree appointing him Shogun while still in his own residence. It was heard that the Imperial Envoy was Sato no Ason Nakahara Yasusuke. On the 14th day of the 10th month, he descended to the Kantō region. The War Commander declared, 'Although Yoritomo has received imperial displeasure in recent years, now that his reputation for martial valor has grown, he receives the Imperial Decree appointing him Shogun while still in his own residence. How should we, as private individuals, accept and present it? Let it be done at the shrine of Wakamiya.' So he went to Wakamiya. Hachiman was established at Tsurugaoka. The terrain was no different from Ishizu, with a surrounding corridor, a two-story gate, and a road descending from over ten cho. 'Indeed, who should accept and present the Imperial Decree?' they deliberated. Miura no Sukke Yoshizumi should accept and present it. The reason was that he was a descendant of Miura no Daitaro Tsunetsugu, who was known for his archery throughout the eight provinces. Moreover, his father, the Great Commander, was a warrior who sacrificed his life for the Lord, so it was heard that this was done to illuminate the dark underworld of the other world for Yoshizumi. The Imperial Envoy Yasusuke, appointed for the Imperial Decree, had two household servants and ten attendants prepared. The Imperial Decree was placed in a document bag, and colorful silk was hung around the neck. Miura no Sukke Yoshizumi also had two household servants and ten attendants prepared. The two household servants were Wada no Saburō Munenari and Hiki no Fujishirō Yoshie. The ten attendants were made up of ten great nobles, each dressed in a hurry. On that day, Miura no Sukke wore a red hakata no hitatare, a black silk-laced armor, carried a great sword made by Ikata, bore twenty-four large black arrows, and had a Shitō bow tucked at his side. He took off his armor, hung it on a high cord, bent his waist, and accepted the Imperial Decree. Yasusuke said, 'Who is the person who will accept and present the Imperial Decree? State your name.' So he did not state his name as Miura no Sukke, but rather stated his true name as Miura no Arakiji Yoshizumi. The Imperial Decree was placed in a lacquer box. It was presented to the War Commander. After a short while, the lacquer box was returned. Since it was heavy, Yasusuke opened it to see, and it contained one hundred ryō of gold dust. At the Wakamiya worship hall, Yasusuke was offered sake. Saiin no Jikan Chikayoshi served the meal. One person of the Fifth Rank performed the role of escort. Three horses were led. One horse had a saddle placed on it. The Great Palace's samurai Kano no Kudo Ichiro Sukeharu led it. An old thatched hut was prepared, and there it was placed. Two layers of thick cotton clothing were set inside a small sleeve box, and a thousand pieces of indigo-dyed white cloth were piled up. The cups and plates were abundant and beautiful.

text: 次の日兵衞佐の館へ向ふ。内外に侍あり、共に十六間也。外侍には家子郎等、肩を竝べ膝を組でなみ居たり。内侍には一門の源氏上座して、末座には大名小名次居たり。源氏の座上に泰定を居らる。良有て寢殿へ向ふ。廣廂に紫縁の疊を敷いて、泰定を居らる。上には高麗縁の疊を敷御簾高く揚させて、兵衞佐殿出られたり。布衣に立烏帽子也。顏大に背低かりけり。容貌優美にして言語分明也。まづ子細を一々のべ給ふ。「平家頼朝が威勢に恐て、都を落ぬ。其の跡に木曾冠者、十郎藏人打入て、我高名顏に、官加階を思ふ樣に成り、剩へ國を嫌ひ申す條奇怪也。奧の秀衡が陸奧守になり、佐竹四郎隆義が常陸守に成て候とて頼朝が命に從はず。急ぎ追討すべき由の院宣を給はるべう候。」左史生申けるは、「今度泰定も名簿參らすべう候が御使で候へば、先づ罷上てやがて認て參すべう候。弟で候ふ史の大夫重能も其儀を申候。」兵衞佐笑て、「當時頼朝が身として、各の名簿思もよらず。さりながらげにも申されば、さこそ存ぜめ。」とぞ宣ひける。やがて今日上洛すべき由申す。今日ばかりは逗留あるべしとて留らる。

annotation.translation: The next day, [they] headed for the residence of Heiwa-no-suke. There were retainers inside and outside, totaling sixteen men. The outer retainers were house servants and attendants, sitting shoulder to shoulder with legs crossed. Among the inner retainers, the Genji clan of the same lineage took the upper seat, while the great lords and their subordinates took the lower seats. Taishō was seated upon the Genji's raised platform. Yoshihira then went toward the sleeping quarters. In the wide corridor, mats with purple borders were laid out, and Taishō was seated there. Above, mats with Korean borders were laid, and the curtain was raised high, allowing Heiwa-no-suke to emerge. He wore a robe of cloth and a black lacquered cap. His face was large, his back slightly bent. His appearance was elegant and refined, and his speech was clear and distinct. First, he recounted the details one by one. "The Taira clan, fearing the might of Yoritomo, has abandoned the capital. In their wake, the Kiso Gōja and Jūrō Zōnin have broken in, appearing as though they seek official rank and promotion, while showing a strange disdain for the realm. It is peculiar that Hidehira of the north has become the Governor of Mutsu, and that Satake no Shirō Takayoshi has become the Governor of Hitachi, yet they do not obey Yoritomo's command. The Emperor should issue an urgent imperial edict ordering their immediate suppression." The scribe replied, "Since Your Excellency is the imperial envoy this time, it would be fitting for Taishō to be included in the register as well. Therefore, we shall first depart and promptly return with confirmation. My younger brother, the Chief of the Historical Bureau, Shōnō, will also report on this matter." Heiwa-no-suke laughed and said, "Back then, Yoritomo, as a person, did not even think of such a list. However, since you have spoken thus, I must indeed remember it." Then, he immediately announced that he should go to the capital today. They decided to stay for today, saying, "There should be no delay today."

text: 次の日兵衞佐の館へ向ふ。萌黄絲威の腹卷一兩、白う作たる太刀一振、滋籐の弓野矢副てたぶ。馬十三匹引る。三匹に鞍置たり。家子郎等十二人に、直垂、小袖、大口、馬鞍に及び、荷懸駄三十匹有けり。鎌倉出の宿より鏡宿に至るまで、宿々十石づゝの米を置かる。澤山なるに依て、施行に引けるとぞ聞えし。

annotation.translation: The next day, they headed for the residence of Hideoza. They had one pair of yellow silk-laced abdominal armor, one white-hilted sword, and a set of arrows for a reed-lashed bow. They led thirteen horses, three of which were saddled. For the twelve house-servants, they provided juppei, kosode, kuchi-bukuro, horse saddles, and thirty packhorses laden with goods. From the inn in Kamakura to the inn at Kagami, they left ten koku of rice at each inn. Because there were so many, they were said to have taken them for the ceremony.

text: 泰定都へ上り、院參して、御坪の内にして、關東の樣具に奏聞しければ、法皇も御感有けり、公卿殿上人も皆ゑつぼにいり給へり。兵衞佐はかうこそゆゝしくおはしけるに、木曾左馬頭都の守護して在ける立居の振舞の無骨さ、もの云詞續の頑なる事限なし。理哉、二歳より信濃國木曾といふ山里に三十迄住馴たりしかば爭かよかるべき。或時猫間中納言光高卿といふ人。木曾に宣ひ合すべき事有て坐たりけり。郎等共「猫間殿の見參に入り申べき事ありとて入せ給ひて候。」と申ければ、木曾大に笑て、「猫は人に見參するか。」「是は猫間中納言殿と申公卿で渡せ給ふ。御宿所の名と覺え候。」と申ければ、木曾「さらば」とて對面す。猶も猫間殿とはえいはで、「猫殿のまれ／＼わいたるに物よそへ。」とぞ宣ひける。中納言是を聞て「只今あるべうもなし。」と宣へば、「いかゞけときにわいたるに、さてはあるべき。」何も新き物を無鹽といふと心得て「こゝに無鹽の平茸有り、とう／＼。」と急がす。根井小彌太陪膳す。田舎合子の極て大にくぼかりけるに、飯堆くよそひ、御菜三種して、平茸の汁で參せたり。木曾が前にも同じ體にて居たりけり。木曾箸取て食す。猫間殿は、合子のいぶせさに、召ざりければ、「其は義仲が精進合子ぞ。」中納言召でもさすが、あしかるべければ、箸取て食由しけり。木曾是を見て、「猫殿は小食におはしけるや。きこゆる猫おろしし給ひたり。かい給へ。」とぞ責たりける。中納言殿、か樣の事に興醒て宣ひ合すべき事も、一言も出さず、軈て急ぎ歸られけり。

annotation.translation: He ascended to the capital in Taishō, paid his respects to the retired emperor, and within the imperial enclosure, reported to the court the manner of affairs in the eastern provinces. The Dharma Emperor was deeply moved, and all the court nobles and high-ranking monks were thoroughly impressed. The Heian no Suketaka was a truly noble and dignified person; however, Kiso no Saemon-no-jo, who was stationed in the capital as its guardian, was characterized by a complete lack of refinement in his conduct, and there was no limit to his obstinacy in speech and argument. Indeed, he had lived in the mountainous region of Kiso in Shinano Province from the age of two until he was thirty, so how could he have become so refined? At one time, a certain man named Neko-no-Kyō, the Chūnagon (Middle Counselor) Mitsutaka, was seated with Kiso to discuss some matter. The retainers said, "Lord Neko is here to pay his respects." Kiso laughed loudly and said, "Do cats pay their respects to humans?" The retainers replied, "This is Lord Neko, the Middle Counselor Mitsutaka, a court noble who has come to visit. Please remember his name as the name of his lodging." Upon hearing this, Kiso said, "Very well," and received him in audience. Even then, he did not address him as "Lord Neko," but said, "As Lord Cat has graciously deigned to visit, prepare some refreshments." Upon hearing this, the Chūnagon replied, "There is nothing available at this very moment." Kiso pressed, "Why, then, do you say you have nothing when he has so graciously come? You must have something." Assuming that "nothing" meant "saltless," he quickly added, "There is a saltless mushroom here, please eat it." Nii no Komata served the meal. The rustic lacquer bowl was extremely large and deeply hollowed; rice was piled high, three vegetable dishes were arranged, and a soup of the saltless mushroom was served. The same was placed before Kiso. Kiso took his chopsticks and began to eat. Lord Neko, seeing the rustic nature of the bowl, did not eat. "That is the ascetic bowl of Yoshinaka," he said. Although the Chūnagon felt it was improper to refuse, he took his chopsticks and ate. Seeing this, Kiso said, "Lord Cat eats only a little, does he? The cat that is heard has been stripped of its fur; please eat it," and thus reproached him. The Chūnagon, disheartened by such behavior, did not utter a single word of the matter they had come to discuss and soon hurriedly returned home.

text: 木曾は、官加階したる者の、直垂で出仕せん事有べうもなかりけりとて、始て布衣とり、裝束烏帽子きはより指貫のすそまで、誠に頑なり。され共車にこのみのんぬ。鎧取て著、矢掻負ひ、弓持て、馬に乘たるには似もにず惡かりけり。牛車は八島の大臣殿の牛車也。牛飼もそれなりけり。世にしたがふ習ひなれば、とらはれてつかはれけれども、あまりのめざましさに、すゑ飼うたる牛の逸物なるが、門出る時、一標當たらうに、なじかはよかるべき。飛で出るに木曾車の内にて、あふのけに倒れぬ。蝶の羽を廣げたる樣に、左右の袖をひろげて、起む／＼とすれども、なじかは起きらるべき。木曾牛飼とはえ言で、「やれ小牛健兒、やれ小牛健兒。」といひければ、車をやれといふと心得て、五六町こそあがかせたれ。今井四郎兼平鞭鐙を合て、追附て、「如何に御車をばかうは仕るぞ。」と呵りければ、「御牛の鼻が強う候。」とぞのべたりける。牛飼中直せんとや思ひけん、「其に候手がたに取著せ給へ。」と申ければ、木曾手がたに無手と取著て、「あはれ支度や、是は牛健兒がはからひか、殿の樣か。」とぞ問うたりける。さて院御所に參著き、車かけはづさせ、後より下んとしければ、京の者の雜色に使はれけるが、「車は、召され候時こそ後より召され候へ。下させ給ふには前よりこそ下させ給へ。」と申けれども、「爭で車ならんからに、すどほりをばすべき。」とて、終に後より下てけり。其外をかしき事共多かりけれども、恐て是を申さず。

annotation.translation: Kiso, though he was an official who had been promoted, was said to have no intention of serving in a hitatare; thus, for the first time, he donned a commoner's robe, from the kosode to the hem of the sleeveless jacket, and was truly stubborn. However, he was not used to riding in a carriage. He put on armor, carried a quiver, held a bow, and mounted a horse, but he looked neither like a warrior nor like a nobleman; it was terrible. The ox cart was that of the Minister of the Eight Islands. The ox driver was the same. Since it was the custom of the world to follow the lead, even if he were captured and sent, the sheer strangeness of the situation was overwhelming. The ox, which had been raised by the driver, was a wild beast; when they left the gate, it was as if it would charge at the first obstacle. Would it be possible to make it go forward? It would not fall backward within Kiso's carriage, even if it were to leap forward like a butterfly spreading its wings; though it would try to rise up and down, would it be possible to make it rise? Kiso's ox driver shouted, 'Oh, strong young ox! Oh, strong young ox!' and, understanding that he was being told to move the carriage, he made it go forward for about five or six cho. Imai no Shiro Kaneyori struck the stirrups with his whip and caught up, scolding, 'How dare you drive the carriage in such a manner?' 'The nose of our ox is strong,' he replied. Thinking perhaps that the ox driver might try to correct the situation, he said, 'Please take hold of the reins.' Kiso, who was completely inexperienced, took hold of them and asked, 'Oh, what a strange preparation! Is this the planning of the strong young ox, or of the lord?' Then, upon arriving at the Imperial residence, they made him dismount from the rear of the carriage. Since he was employed as a low-ranking official in Kyoto, he said, 'When the carriage is summoned, it should be summoned from the rear; when it is to be dismounted, it should be dismounted from the front.' However, they replied, 'Why, if it is a carriage, it must be dismounted from the side,' and finally, they made him dismount from the rear. There were many other strange incidents, but I fear to mention them all.

text: 平家は讃岐の八島に有ながら、山陽道八箇國、南海道六箇國、都合十四箇國をぞ討取ける。木曾左馬頭是を聞き、安からぬ事也とて、やがて討手を差遣す。討手の大將には矢田判官代義清、侍大將には、信濃國の住人海野彌平四郎行廣、都合其勢七千餘騎山陽道へ馳下り、備中國水島が渡に舟を浮べて、八島へ既に寄んとす。

annotation.translation: Although the Taira were stationed at Yashima in Sanuki, they attacked and captured a total of fourteen provinces: the eight provinces of the San'yōdō and the six provinces of the Nankaidō. Upon hearing of this, Kiso no Sa-matō thought it an alarming matter and immediately dispatched an attacking force. The commander of the attacking force was Yada no Hangan-dai Yoshiyoshi, and the samurai commander was Uno Yabē Shirō Yukihiro, a resident of Shinano Province; with a total force of over seven thousand cavalry, they hastened down the San'yōdō, set their boats afloat at the water crossing of Mizushima in Bitchū Province, and were already about to arrive at Yashima.

text: 同閏十月一日、水島が渡に小船一艘出來たり。海士船釣船かと見る程に、さはなくして、平家方より牒の使船也。是を見て、源氏の舟五百餘艘ほしあげたるををめき叫んで下けり。平家は千餘艘でおし寄たり。平家の方の大手の大將軍には新中納言知盛卿、搦手の大將軍には能登守教經也。能登殿宣ひけるは、「如何に者共、いくさをばゆるに仕るぞ。北國の奴原に生捕られんをば、心憂とは思はずや。御方の船をば組や。」とて、千餘艘が艫綱舳綱を組合せ、中にもやひを入れ、歩の板を引渡いたれば、船の上は平々たり。源平兩方鬨を作り、矢合して、互に舟ども推合せて責戰ふ。遠きをば弓で射、近きをば太刀で切り、熊手に懸て取もあり、取るゝもあり。引組て海に入もあり。刺違へて、死ぬるもあり。思ひ／＼心々に勝負をす。源氏の方の侍大將海野彌平四郎討れにけり。是を見て大將軍矢田判官代義清主從七人小舟に乘て、眞先に進で戰ふ程に、如何したりけん、船踏沈て皆死ぬ。平家は鞍置馬を船の中に立られたりければ、船差寄せ馬共引下し、打乘／＼をめいて懸ければ、源氏の勢大將軍は討れぬ。我先にとぞ落行ける。平家は水島の軍に勝てこそ、會稽の恥をば雪けれ。

annotation.translation: On the same day, the 1st of the intercalary 10th month, a small boat appeared at the water crossing of Mizushima. It looked like a fisherman's boat or a fishing boat, but in fact it was a messenger boat from the Taira clan. Seeing this, the Minamoto forces, having raised over five hundred boats, raised their voices and rushed down. The Taira forces arrived with over a thousand boats. The great general of the main force of the Taira side was the newly appointed Chancellor of the Right, Lord Tomomori; the great general of the rear guard was the Governor of Noto, Nobutaka. Lord Noto declared, "How can these fellows allow themselves to fight? Do you not fear being captured alive on the plains of the Northern Country? Join the boats of your own side." Thus, they tied together the stern ropes and bow ropes of over a thousand boats, placed planks in the middle, and passed over walking boards, so that the tops of the ships became flat and level. Both the Minamoto and Taira sides raised their war cries, exchanged arrows, and pushed their ships against one another in battle. Those at a distance were shot with bows, those close were cut with swords, some were caught with grappling hooks and taken, others were taken without such means. Some were drawn into the sea, others were pierced through and died. Each person, according to their own mind, fought for victory. The Minamoto's great general, the samurai Taishō of the Ueno family, Hiromi no Yūhei, was slain. Seeing this, the great general Yada no Hangan-no-dai, Yoshikiyo, along with his retainers, seven men in total, boarded a small boat and charged ahead to fight. Somehow, the boat was trampled and sank, and all of them drowned. Because the Taira had placed saddled horses inside their ships, they lowered the horses, had them leap aboard, and struck fear into the enemy. The Minamoto's great general was not slain, but they fled, each trying to escape first. Thus, the Taira won the battle at Mizushima, and the shame of Kuji was washed away.

text: 木曾左馬頭是をきゝ、安からぬ事也とて、一萬騎で山陽道へ馳下る。平家の侍備中國住人瀬尾太郎兼康は、北國の戰ひに、加賀國の住人藏光次郎成澄が手にかゝて、生捕にせられたりしを、成澄が弟藏光三郎成氏に預けられたり。きこゆる剛の者大力なりければ、木曾殿あたらをのこを失ふべきかとて切らず、人あひ心樣優に情ありければ、藏光も懇にもてなしけり。蘇子卿が胡國に囚はれ、李少卿が漢朝へ歸らざりしが如し。遠く異國につける事は、昔の人の悲めりし處也と云へり。韋鞴毳幕、以て風雨を禦ぎ、羶肉酪漿、以て飢渇に充つ。夜は寢事なく、晝は終日につかへ、木を伐草を刈ずと云ふ許に從ひつゝ、如何にもして敵を窺ひ討て、今一度舊主を見奉らんと、思ひける兼康が、心の程こそ怖けれ。

annotation.translation: Kiso no Samanokami, having heard this, thought it was a matter of no peace and, with ten thousand cavalry, rushed down the Sanyō Road. The Heike retainer Seko Tarō Kaneyasu, a resident of Bitchū Province, had previously been captured alive by Kuramitsurō Narumi, a resident of Kaga Province, during a battle in the northern region, and was entrusted to Kuramitsurō's younger brother, Kuramitsurō Narishige. Since he was known as a mighty and powerful man, Lord Kiso, fearing he might lose his life, chose not to execute him; moreover, because the man's disposition was gentle and full of compassion, Kuramitsura treated him with great hospitality. It was like Su Zijiang being imprisoned in the Hu region and Li Shaojiang failing to return to the Han court. To be far away in a foreign land is said to be a sorrow that ancient people have mourned. With leather saddles and felt tents, they ward off wind and rain; with mutton, curdled milk, and yogurt, they satisfy hunger and thirst. At night there is no sleep, and by day they are occupied from dawn to dusk, following the commands to cut wood and cut grass. Yet, how he thought, plotting in every way to spy on and attack the enemy, hoping to see his old lord once more, is indeed a matter of terror for the heart.

text: 或時瀬尾太郎藏光三郎に逢うて云ひけるは、「去ぬる五月よりかひなき命を助けられ參せて候へば、誰をたれとか思ひ參せ候べき。自今以後御軍候はゞ、ま先かけて木曾殿に命を參せん。兼康が知行仕り候し備中の瀬尾は、馬の草飼好い處で候。御邊申て給らせ給へ。」といひければ、藏光この樣を申す。木曾殿「神妙の事を申すごさんなれ。さらば汝瀬尾を案内者にして先づ下れ。誠に馬の草なんどをも構へさせよ。」と宣へば、藏光三郎畏り悦んで其勢三十騎ばかり、兼康を先として備中へぞ下ける。瀬尾が嫡子小太郎宗康は、平家の御方に候けるが、父が木曾殿より暇ゆるされて下ると聞えしかば、年比の郎等共催し聚め、其勢五十騎許迎に上る程に、播磨の國府で行あうて下る。備前國三石の宿に留またりければ、瀬尾が親き者共、酒を持せて出來たり。其終夜悦の酒盛しけるに、あづかりの武士、藏光三郎所從ともに三千餘人強伏て起しも立ず、一々に皆刺殺てけり。備前國は十郎藏人の國也。其代官の國府に有けるをも、押寄て討てけり。「兼康こそ暇賜て罷下れ、平家に志思ひ參せん人々は、兼康を先として木曾殿の下り給に矢一つ射懸奉れ。」と披露しければ、備前、備中、備後三箇國の兵共馬物具然るべき所從をば、平家の御方へ参せて、息みける老者共、或はかきの直垂につめ紐し、或は布の小袖に東折し、くさり腹卷綴り著て、山靱、高箙に矢共少々差し、掻負掻負瀬尾が許へ馳集る。都合其勢二千餘人、瀬尾太郎を先とし、備前國福龍寺繩手の篠の迫を城郭に構へ、口二丈深さ二丈に堀を掘り、逆茂木引高矢倉あげ、かい楯かき、矢先を汰へて今や／＼と待かけたり。

annotation.translation: At one time, he met Seo Taro Kura Mitsujiro and said, 'Since my worthless life has been saved and I have been allowed to live since last May, whom could I possibly think of serving? From now on, if Your Excellency are to engage in war, I shall first dedicate my life to Lord Kiso. The land of Bizen, Seo, which was held by Kanehira, is a place good for feeding horses. I beg you to send troops.' Upon hearing this, Kura Mitsujiro said as follows. Lord Kiso said, 'You speak a divine matter. Very well, let you be the guide to Seo, and go down first. Truly, I shall have you prepare even horse fodder.' When he said this, Kura Mitsujiro, filled with awe and joy, led about thirty horsemen, with Kanehira in the lead, and went down to Bizen. The eldest son of Seo, Kotaro Munesada, was on the side of the Taira family. Hearing that his father had been granted leave by Lord Kiso and was going down, he gathered and assembled his retainers as before. When he had gathered about fifty horsemen and went up to meet them, they met at the Kokufu of Harima Province. Since they stayed at the lodging of Mitsuishi in Bizen Province, the close associates of Seo came with wine. They drank all night in merriment. The samurai who had come to help, along with Kura Mitsujiro's followers, numbered over three thousand; they lay in ambush and did not rise or stand up, but killed them all one by one. Bizen Province is the province of the Tenth Clerk. They attacked and defeated the kokushi who was stationed at the Kokufu as his deputy. They announced, 'Kanehira alone has been granted leave and has gone down. As for those who wish to serve the Taira family, they shall shoot one arrow at Lord Kiso as he goes down, with Kanehira in the lead.' When this was proclaimed, the warriors of the three provinces of Bizen, Bitchu, and Bingo, along with their retainers who had appropriate armor, went over to the Taira side. The old men who were panting, some wore black dirks with their belts tied, others wore blue short-sleeved coats with eastern folds, and fastened chain cuirasses. They carried a few arrows in mountain quivers and high quivers, and, carrying and carrying, rushed to gather at Seo's place. In total, about two thousand men, with Seo Taro in the lead, constructed a fortress at the bamboo thicket of the rope hand of Foryu-ji in Bizen Province. They dug a moat two jo wide and two jo deep, raised high palisades and arrow towers, built shields with sharp edges, and trimmed the arrowheads, waiting anxiously, one after another.

text: 備前の國に十郎藏人の置かれたりし代官、瀬尾に討たれて、其下人共が逃て京へ上る程に、播磨と備前の境船坂といふ處にて、木曾殿に參りあふ。此由申ければ、木曾殿、「やすからぬ。斬て捨べかりつる物を。」と後悔せられければ、今井四郎申けるは、「さ候へばこそ、きやつが面魂たゝ者とは見え候はず、千度斬うと申候つる者を、扶けさせ給て。」と申。「思ふに何程の事か在るべき。逐懸て討て。」とぞ宣ひける。今井四郎「まづ下て見候はん。」とて、三千餘騎で、馳下る。福龍寺繩手は、はたばり弓杖一たけばかりにて、遠さは西國道一里也。左右は深田にて、馬の足も及ねば、三千餘騎が心は先に進めども馬次第にぞ歩せける。兼平押寄せて見ければ、瀬尾太郎矢倉に立出で、大音聲を揚て、「去ぬる五月より今までかひなき命を助けられて候各の御芳志は、是をこそ用意仕て候へ。」とて、究竟の強弓精兵數百人勝り聚め、矢先を汰へて指詰引詰散々に射る。面を向くべき樣もなし。今井四郎を始として楯、禰井、宮崎三郎、諏訪、藤澤などいふはやりをの兵共、甲の錣を傾けて射殺さるゝ人馬を取入れ引入れ堀を埋め、をめき叫んで責戰ふ。或は左右の深田に打入れて馬のくさわきむながいつくし、太腹などに立處を事ともせず、むらめかいて寄せ、或は谷ふけをも嫌はず、懸入々々一日戰ひ暮しけり。夜に入りて瀬尾が催し集めたる驅武者共、皆責落されて助る者は少う討るる者ぞ多かりける。瀬尾太郎篠の迫の城郭を破られて、引退き、備中國板倉河の端に、掻楯かいて待懸たり。今井四郎やがて押寄せ攻ければ、山靱竹箙に矢種の有程こそ防ぎけれ、皆射盡してければ、我先にとぞ落行ける。瀬尾太郎たゞ主從三騎に打なされ、板倉河の端に著て、みとろ山の方へ落行く程に北國で、瀬尾生捕にしたりし藏光次郎成澄、弟は討れぬ。「安からぬ事なり。瀬尾に於ては、又生捕に仕候はん。」とて、群に拔て追て行く。あはひ一町許に追附て、「如何に瀬尾殿、正なうも敵に後をば見する者哉。返せや返せ。」といはれ、板倉河を西へ渡す、河中に引へて待かけたり。藏光、馳來て押竝べてむずと組で、どうと落つ。互に劣ぬ大力なれば、上になり、下になり、ころびあふ程に、河岸に淵の有けるに轉入て、藏光は無水練也、瀬尾は勝れたる水練なりければ水の底で藏光を取て押へ、鎧の草摺引上、柄も拳も透れ／＼と三刀刺いて頸をとる。我馬は乘損じたれば、敵藏光が馬に乘て落行ほどに、瀬尾が嫡子小太郎宗康馬にはのらず、歩行にて郎等つれて落行程に、未だ、年は二十二三の男なれども、餘に太て、一町ともえ走ず。物具ぬきすてゝ歩めども叶はざりけり。父は是をうち捨て、十餘町こそ逃延たれ。郎等に逢うていひけるは、「兼康日來は千萬の敵に向て軍するは、四方晴て覺るが、今度は小太郎を捨て行ばにや、一向先が暗うて見えぬぞ。縦兼康命生て、再平家の御方へ参たりとも、同隷ども『兼康今は六十にあまりたる者の、幾程の命を惜うで、唯獨ある子を捨て落けるやらん。』と言はむ事こそ慚かしけれ。」郎等申けるは、「さ候へばこそ、御一所で如何にも成せ給へと申つるはこゝ候。かへさせ給へ。」と云ひければ、「さらば。」とて取て回す。小太郎は、足かばかり腫て伏り。「汝が得逐付かねば、一處で討死せうとて歸たるは如何に。」と云へば、小太郎涙をはらはらと流いて、「此身こそ無器量の者で候へば自害をも仕候べきに、我故御命をさへ失なひ參せん事、五逆罪にや候はんずらん。唯とう／＼延させ給へ。」と申せども、「思ひ切たる上は。」とて、息む處に、今井四郎ま先懸て其勢五十騎ばかりをめいて追懸たり。瀬尾太郎矢七つ八つ射殘したるを、差詰引詰散々に射る。死生は知らず矢庭に敵五六騎射落す。其後打物拔て、先小太郎が首討落し、敵の中へ破て入り散々に戰ひ、敵あまた討取て、終に討死してけり。郎等も主にちとも劣ず戰ひけるが、大事の手あまた負ひ戰ひ疲れて、自害せんとしけるが、生捕にこそせられけれ。中一日有て死にけり。是等主從三人が首をば、備中國鷺が森にぞ懸たりける。木曾殿是を見給ひて「あはれ剛の者哉。是をこそ一人當千の兵とも云ふべけれ。あたら者共を扶けて見で。」とぞ宣ひける。

annotation.translation: In the time when a governor was stationed in Bizen Province, he was defeated and killed by Seo at Seo. As his retainers fled and made their way up to the capital, they met Lord Kiso at a place called Funasaka, the border between Harima and Bizen. When they reported this, Lord Kiso said, "This is not right. I had intended to cut them down and discard them." Regretting this, Imai Shiro said, "If that is the case, then the man whose face and spirit are as noble as his would not have been seen. The one who claimed he would cut him a thousand times, please have him rescued." Lord Kiso declared, "There must be some significance to this. Pursue and defeat them." Imai Shiro said, "First, let us go down and see." They descended with over three thousand cavalry. The rope-hand of Fukuryu-ji was merely a single bow-length long, and the distance was one ri along the Western Road. On both sides were deep marshes where horses' hooves could not reach; although the hearts of the three thousand cavalry urged them forward, their horses moved according to the terrain. Kanesue approached and saw that Seo Taro stood up from his arrow-rack, raised a great voice, and said, "Since last May until now, you have been spared a futile life. Please prepare for this." Gathering several hundred elite archers and strong soldiers, he aimed his arrows, drew his bowstrings tightly, and rained arrows everywhere. There was no way to face them. Starting with Imai Shiro, the warriors bearing shields, Nei, Miyazaki Saburo, Suwa, Fujisawa, and others, leaning their helmet crests, shot down men and horses, taking their armor and bodies, filling the moats with them, shouting and charging fiercely. Some charged into the deep marshes on both sides, causing the horses to stumble and fall, not minding wounds on their bellies or other places, swarming and pressing forward. Others did not avoid even the valley bottoms, fighting day after day until nightfall. When night came, the mounted warriors summoned by Seo Taro were all driven back; few escaped, while many were killed. Seo Taro's fortress at Shino-zaka was breached. He withdrew and waited at the bank of the Itakura River in Bitchu Province, raising a shield. Imai Shiro soon advanced and attacked. As long as there were arrows in his bamboo quiver, he held his ground, but once all his arrows were exhausted, they fled one after another. Seo Taro was left with only his lord and retainer, three riders. Reaching the bank of the Itakura River, he began to flee toward Mitoro Mountain. In the Northern Country, Kurokoji Narumi, whom Seo had captured alive, was killed by his brother. "This is not right," he said. "At Seo, I was captured alive again." Breaking from the group, he pursued. After chasing about a town's distance, he caught up and said, "How can Lord Seo, without a doubt, turn his back to the enemy? Return, return!" They forced him to cross the Itakura River to the west and held him in the middle of the river. Kurokoji galloped up, grappled with him, and they both fell. Since they were equally powerful, they rolled over each other, rising and falling, until they tumbled into a deep pool by the riverbank. Kurokoji was an expert swimmer, and Seo was even more skilled. At the bottom of the water, Kurokoji seized and held down Seo, pulling up his armor's hem, piercing through the hilt and the fist, stabbing three times, and cutting off his neck. Since his own horse was damaged, he mounted Seo's horse and fled. Seo's eldest son, Kotaro Mune-yasu, did not mount a horse but fled on foot with his retainers. Although he was a man of twenty or twenty-three years, he was so fat that he could not run even a town's distance. Even throwing away his armor and equipment, he could not escape. His father abandoned him, fleeing for over ten towns. When he met his retainers, he said, "Kanesue has fought against countless enemies these past days, and the four directions have cleared and become bright. But this time, if I abandon Kotaro, the path ahead seems completely dark. Even if Kanesue survives and returns to serve the Heike clan, my fellow retainers will say, 'Kanesue is now over sixty years old. Why would he spare his life and abandon his only son?' Such words would be shameful." The retainers replied, "That is why we have been urging you to take him with us and survive together. Please return with him." Hearing this, he said, "Very well," and turned back. Kotaro's legs were swollen, and he was lying down. "If you cannot escape, it would be better to die together here," he said. Kotaro shed tears profusely and said, "I am an unworthy person, and I should commit suicide. But to lose my life because of me would be a five-fold sin. Please let me live." However, with a resolute heart, he said, "Since I have made up my mind." While he was catching his breath, Imai Shiro, leading a vanguard of about fifty riders, pursued them. Seo Taro still had seven or eight arrows left. He drew them tightly and shot them wildly. Not knowing life or death, he shot down five or six enemy riders in the midst of the battle. Afterward, he drew his sword, beheaded the first enemy (Kotaro), broke through the enemy ranks, fought fiercely, killed many enemies, and finally died in battle. The retainers fought as bravely as their lord, but after suffering many wounds and growing exhausted, they attempted to commit suicide but were captured alive. One day later, they died. The heads of these three, lord and retainers, were hung at Shiga-mori in Bitchu Province. Lord Kiso, seeing this, said, "Truly, they are valiant men. They can be called a thousand men each. Have the wounded brought here and shown to me."

text: さる程に木曾殿は備中國萬壽の庄にて勢汰へして、八島へ既に寄むとす。其間都の留守に置かれたる樋口次郎兼光、使者を立てて、「十郎藏人殿こそ殿のましまさぬ間に、院のきり人して、樣々に讒奏せられ候なれ。西國の軍をば暫指置せ給て、急ぎ上せ給へ。」と申ければ、木曾「さらば」とて夜を日に繼で馳上る。十郎藏人あしかりなんとやおもひけむ。木曾にちがはむと丹波路に懸て播磨へ下る。木曾は攝津國を經て都へ入る。

annotation.translation: Thus, Lord Kiso was stationed at Manju no Shō in Bitchū Province and was already preparing to go to Yashima. Meanwhile, Higuchi no Jirō Kanehira, who had been left in charge in the capital, sent a messenger, saying, "Lord Tōrō Kurōdono, during His Lordship's absence, various slanderous reports have been made to the Emperor; please hold the western army for a while and come up quickly." Upon hearing this, Kiso replied, "Very well," and rode day and night. What could Tōrō Kurō have thought but that Kiso was acting wrongly? He took the path through Tango and descended to Harima. Kiso passed through Settsu Province and entered the capital.

text: 平家は又木曾討むとて、大將軍には新中納言知盛卿、本三位中將重衡卿、侍大將には、越中次郎兵衞盛嗣、上總五郎兵衞忠光、惡七兵衞景清、伊賀平内左衞門家長、都合其勢二萬餘騎千餘艘の舟に乘り播磨の地へ押渡りて、室山に陣をとる。十郎藏人、平家と軍して木曾と中直せんとや思ひけむ。其勢五百餘騎で室山へこそ押寄せたれ。平家は陣を五つに張る。一陣越中次郎兵衞盛嗣二千餘騎、二陣、伊賀平内左衞門家長二千餘騎、三陣、上總五郎兵衞忠光、惡七兵衞景清、三千餘騎、四陣、本三位中將重衡卿三千餘騎、五陣、新中納言知盛卿一萬餘騎でかためらる。十郎藏人行家五百餘騎でをめいて懸く。一陣越中次郎兵衞盛嗣、暫く會釋う樣に持成いて、中を颯と開けて通す。二陣伊賀平内左衞門家長、同じう明けて通しけり。三陣上總五郎兵衞、惡七兵衞共に明けて通しけり。四陣本三位中將重衡卿是も明て入れられけり。一陣より五陣迄、兼て約束したりければ、敵を中に取籠て、一度に鬨をどとぞ作りける。十郎藏人今は逃るべき方も無りければ、たばかられぬと思ひて、面も振ず、命も惜まず、爰を最後と攻戰ふ。平家の侍共、「源氏の大將に組めや。」とて我先に進めども、さすが十郎藏人に押並べて組む武者一騎も無りけり。新中納言の宗と憑まれたりける紀七左衞門、紀八衞門、紀九郎など云ふ兵共、そこにて皆十郎藏人に討取らる。かくして十郎藏人五百餘騎が、僅に三十騎許に討成され、四方は皆敵也、御方は無勢也。如何にして逃べしとは覺ねど、思ひ切て、雲霞の如くなる敵の中を破て通る。されども、我身は手も負はず、家子郎等廿餘騎大略手負うて、播磨國高砂より船に乘り、おしいだいて和泉國吹飯の浦にぞ著にける。其より河内へ打越えて、長野城に引籠る。平家は室山、水島二箇度の軍に勝てこそ、彌勢は附にけれ。

annotation.translation: The Heike, intending to attack the Kiso forces, stationed the new Chūnagon Tomomori-no-kimi as the Grand General, the former Sanmi no Shō Shōkō-no-kimi as the Main Lieutenant General, and as Attendants-General, Echizen no Jirō Bē Morotsugu, Kazusa no Gorō Bē Tadaatsugu, Akuichi Bē Kiyokiyo, Iga no Hōno Saemon Nagaharu, and others. With a total force of over twenty thousand cavalry and over a thousand ships, they crossed to Harima Province and established their camp at Muroyama. Could the Jūrō Kubo have thought that the Heike would engage the Kiso forces and force them to retreat? Yet the Heike, with only over five hundred cavalry, rushed to Muroyama. The Heike deployed their troops in five lines: the first line, Echizen no Jirō Bē Morotsugu, with over two thousand cavalry; the second line, Iga no Hōno Saemon Nagaharu, with over two thousand cavalry; the third line, Kazusa no Gorō Bē Tadaatsugu and Akuichi Bē Kiyokiyo, with over three thousand cavalry; the fourth line, the former Sanmi no Shō Shōkō-no-kimi, with over three thousand cavalry; and the fifth line, the new Chūnagon Tomomori-no-kimi, with over ten thousand cavalry, thus fortifying their positions. Jūrō Kubo, with over five hundred cavalry, charged at them. The first line, Echizen no Jirō Bē Morotsugu, held the line for a brief moment as if to meet them, then suddenly opened a passage and let them through. The second line, Iga no Hōno Saemon Nagaharu, also opened a passage and let them through. The third line, Kazusa no Gorō Bē and Akuichi Bē, both opened a passage and let them through. The fourth line, the former Sanmi no Shō Shōkō-no-kimi, also opened a passage and allowed them to enter. From the first line to the fifth line, as they had previously agreed, they captured the enemy within and simultaneously raised a mighty battle cry. With no way to escape, Jūrō Kubo, thinking he would not be deceived, did not turn his face away, did not spare his life, and fought on, regarding this place as his last stand. The Heike warriors shouted, "Form ranks against the General of the Minamoto!" and pushed forward one after another, yet not a single warrior was able to engage Jūrō Kubo in close combat. The warriors such as Ki no Shichizōemon, Ki no Hachimōn, and Ki no Kyūrō, who had been possessed by the spirit of the new Chūnagon, were all slain by Jūrō Kubo there. Thus, of Jūrō Kubo's over five hundred cavalry, only about thirty were left alive; all around were enemies, and there were no allies. Though he realized there was no way to escape, with a resolute heart he broke through the enemy like a cloud and made his way through. However, while he himself was not wounded, over twenty of his housemen were injured. They boarded ships from Takasago in Harima Province, rowed hard, and landed at the bay of Aizumi Province, called Fui. From there, they crossed to Kawachi Province and withdrew into Nagano Castle. The Heike, having won at both Muroyama and Mizushima, gained even greater strength.

text:
凡京中には源氏の勢滿々て、在々所々に入取多し。賀茂、八幡の御領とも言はず、青田を刈て馬草にす。人の倉を打開て物を取り、持て通る物を奪取り、衣裳を剥取る。「平家の都におはせし時は、六波羅殿とて、唯おほかた怖しかりし計也。衣裳をはぐ迄はなかりし者を、平家に源氏替へ劣りしたり。」とぞ人申ける。木曾左馬頭の許へ法皇より御使在り。「狼藉靜めよ。」と仰せ下さる。御使は壹岐守知親が子に、壹岐判官知康と云ふ者也。天下に勝れたる鼓の上手で有ければ、時の人鼓判官とぞ申ける。木曾對面して、先づ御返事をば申さで、「抑和殿を鼓判官と云ふは、萬の人に打たれたうか、はられたうか。」とぞ問うたりける。知康返事に及ばず、院の御所に歸り參
て、「義仲嗚呼の者で候[2]唯今朝敵に成候なんず。急ぎ追討せさせ給へ。」と申ければ、法皇軈て思召立せ給ひけり。さらば然るべき武士にも仰附られずして、山の座主寺の長吏に仰られて、山三井寺の惡僧共を召されけり。公卿殿上人の召されける勢と申は、向へ礫、印地、云甲斐なき辻冠者原、乞食法師どもなりけり。

annotation.translation: Generally, in the capital, the power of the Minamoto is overwhelmingly strong, and they take what they want in place after place. They do not even say it is the imperial estate of Kamo or Hachiman; they cut green fields to make horse fodder. They break open people's storehouses to take things, seize goods being carried away, and strip off clothing. 'When the Taira were in the capital, at Rokuhara they were merely feared; they were not the ones who stripped people of their clothes, yet the Minamoto have surpassed the Taira in this.' Thus people said. An imperial messenger came from the Retired Emperor to Kiso no Sakanokami. 'Quell your ravages,' he was ordered. The messenger was the son of the Governor of Iki, known as Iki no Shō no Gōno Toshiyasu. Because he was the finest drummer in the land, the people of the time called him Drum Governor Toshiyasu. Facing Kiso, he first did not reply, but instead asked, 'Pray, when they call Lord Waka the Drum Governor, is it because he was struck hard or beaten severely?' Toshiyasu, unable to answer, returned to the imperial palace and said, 'Yoshitsune is such a man; only this morning he became our enemy. Please hasten to send troops to pursue and destroy him.' The Retired Emperor then immediately resolved. Thus, without even commanding a proper warrior, he was ordered by the head official of the mountain temple to summon the evil monks of Mount Miidera. The force summoned by the high-ranking courtiers and nobles was nothing but a group of ruffians hurling stones, throwing dirt, and the like—worthless crossroad bandits and begging monks.

text: 木曾左馬頭院の御氣色惡うなると聞えしかば、始は木曾に隨うたりける五畿内の者共、皆背いて、院方へ參る。信濃源氏村上の三郎判官代是も木曾を背いて法皇へ參りけり。今井四郎申けるは、「是こそ以の外の御大事で候へ。さればとて十善帝王に向ひ參せて、如何でか御合戰候べき。甲を脱ぎ弓の弦を弛て、降人に參せ給へ。」と申せば、木曾大に怒て、「我信濃を出し時、小見、合田の戰より始めて、北國には、砥浪山、黒坂、鹽坂、篠原、西國には、福龍寺繩手、篠の迫、板倉が城を攻しかども、未だ敵に後を見せず。縱十善帝王にてましますとも、甲を脱ぎ弓の弦を弛いて降人にはえこそ參るまじけれ。譬へば都の守護して有ん者が、馬一疋づゝ飼て乘らざるべきか。幾らも有る田共刈せ馬草にせんを、強に法皇の咎め給ふべき樣や有る。兵粮米もなければ、冠者原共が、片邊に附て、時々入取せんは、何か強僻事ならん。大臣家や宮々の御所へも參らばこそ僻事ならめ。是は鼓判官が凶害と覺ゆるぞ。其鼓め打破て捨よ。今度は義仲が最後の軍にて有んずるぞ。頼朝がかへり聞んずる所も有り。軍ようせよ、者共。」とて打立けり。北國の勢ども皆落下て、僅に六七千騎ぞ有ける。我軍の吉例なればとて、七手に造る。先樋口次郎兼光二千餘騎で、新熊野の方へ搦手に差遣す。殘り六手は、各が居たらんずる條里小路より河原へ出で、七條河原にて一つになれと、相圖を定て出立けり。

annotation.translation: When it was heard that the Left Commander of Kisō-in was in ill health, the men of the Five Provinces who had originally followed Kisō all turned away and went to the side of the Emperor. Even Shino Genji Murakami no Sanrō Jōkan left Kisō and went to the Retired Emperor. Imai no Shirō declared, 'This is indeed an extraordinary matter. Therefore, when you appear before the Ten Virtuous Emperor, how shall you conduct the battle? Take off your armor, slacken your bowstring, and become a surrendering subject.' When he said this, Kisō became greatly angry, saying, 'When I left Shinano, from the Battle of Komi and Aida onward, in the Northern Provinces I besieged Tominami Mountain, Kurosaka, Shiosaka, Shinohara, and in the Western Provinces Fukuryū-ji, Nawa, Shino-no-seki, and the castle of Itakura, yet I have never seen the enemy's back. Even if he is the Ten Virtuous Emperor, I shall not take off my armor, slacken my bowstring, and become a surrendering subject. Suppose someone who guards the capital keeps horses, one by one, and does not ride them? Shall we harvest our abundant fields to feed the horses and be strongly blamed by the Retired Emperor? We have no food or rice, and the warriors will gather on one side and attack from time to time; is that not a strange thing? If we were to go to the residence of the Minister or the palaces of the princes, that would indeed be strange. This appears to be the wickedness of Tsuyuri Jōkan. Break and discard that drum! This is to be Yoshinaka's final campaign. There is a place where Yoritomo may hear of it. Prepare the army, men!' and he stood up. The forces of the Northern Provinces all fell away, and only six or seven thousand cavalry remained. Since this was in accordance with our good custom, we divided into seven divisions. First, Higuchi no Jirō Kanemitsu with over two thousand cavalry was sent to the rear, toward the direction of New Kumano. The remaining six divisions were to emerge from their respective quarters on Jōriji Street to the riverbank, and unite at the Shichijō Riverbank, and thus they fixed their formation and set out.

text: 軍は十一月十九日の朝也。院御所法住寺殿にも、軍兵二萬餘人參籠たる由聞えけり。御方の笠効には松の葉をぞ著たりける。木曾法住寺殿の西門に押寄せて見れば、鼓判官知康、軍の行事承て、赤地の錦の直垂に、鎧は態ど著ざりけり、甲計ぞ著たりける。甲には四天を書て押たりけり。御所の西の築垣の上に登て立たりけるが、片手には鉾を持ち、片手には金剛鈴を以て打振々々、時々は舞折も有けり。若き公卿殿上人「風情なし。知康には天狗ついたり。」とぞ笑はれける。知康大音聲を揚て、「昔は宣旨を向て讀ければ、枯たる草木も花咲き實生り惡鬼惡神も從ひけり。末代ならんからに、如何が十善の帝王に向ひ參せて、弓をば引くべき。汝等が放ん矢は、却て身にあたるべし。拔む太刀は、身を切べし。」などのゝしりければ、木曾「さな謂せそ。」とて、鬨をどと作る。

annotation.translation: The army was on the morning of November 19. It was heard that over twenty thousand soldiers had assembled at the Imperial Palace and the Hōjūji Palace of the Retired Emperor. On the caps of the imperial guards, they had attached pine leaves. When they pressed against the west gate of the Hōjūji Palace of the Kiso clan, one could see that Governor Chikayasu, who was in charge of the army's affairs, was wearing a red brocade hitatare and had not put on his armor; instead, he had donned a kōhei. On his chest plate, he had painted the Four Heavenly Kings. He had climbed onto the earthen wall to the west of the Imperial Palace and stood there; in one hand he held a spear, and in the other he struck and shook a Vajra bell, now and then also dancing. A young noble of high rank said, "How unseemly! Chikayasu must have been possessed by a tengu." When Chikayasu raised his voice loudly, saying, "In the past, when I read the imperial rescript facing the throne, even withered grass and trees would bloom and bear fruit, and evil demons and gods would follow. Since the end times have come, what reason is there for me to approach the Ten-Virtues Emperor and draw my bow? The arrows you release will strike you yourselves. The drawn sword will cut your own bodies." etc., Kiso cried out, "Do not speak such nonsense!" and sounded the war cry, "Doto!"

text: さる程に搦手に差し遣はしたる樋口次郎兼光新熊野の方より、鬨の聲をぞ合せたる。鏑の中に火を入て、法住寺殿の御所に射立てたりければ、折節風は烈しゝ、猛火天に燃上て、焔は虚空に隙もなし。軍の行事知康は、人より先に落にけり。行事が落つる上は、二萬餘人の官軍共、我先にとぞ落ゆきける。餘りに遽噪いで、弓取る者は矢を知らず、矢取る者は弓を知らず。或は長刀倒について、我足つきつらぬく者も有り、或は弓の弭物にかけて、えはづさで捨て迯る者も有り。七條が末は攝津國の源氏の固たりけるが、七條を西へ落て行く。兼て軍以前より「落人の在んずるをば用意して打殺せ。」と御所より披露せられたりければ、在洛の者共、屋根ゐに楯をつき、おそへの石を取聚て、待懸たる處に、攝津國源氏の落けるを、「あはや落人よ。」とて、石を拾かけ、散々に打ければ、「是は院方ぞ、過仕るな。」と云へども、「さな云せそ。院宣であるに、唯打殺せ／＼。」とて打つ間、或は馬を捨て、はふ／＼逃ぐる者もあり。或は打殺るゝ者もありけり。八條が末は山僧固めたりけるが、恥有る者は討死し、強顏者は落ぞ行く。

annotation.translation: In this manner, when Higuchi Jiro Kanehiro was sent to the rear from the direction of the new Kumano, they raised a battle cry together. Since they had put fire into a war-drum and shot it into the Imperial Palace of Emperor Go-Shirakawa, and the wind happened to be fierce at that moment, the fierce fire burned up into the sky, and the flames left no gap in the void. The military commander, Tomoyasu, fell before anyone else. When the commander fell, the more than twenty thousand imperial soldiers all fled, each thinking, "I will go first." They were so utterly panicked that those who drew bows did not know how to shoot arrows, and those who took arrows did not know how to use bows. Some, with their long swords turned backward, pierced their own feet; some, hooking their bow handles, fled without even removing their armor. At the end of Shijo Street, the Minamoto of Settsu Province held their ground, but they were forced to retreat westward from Shijo Street.
